conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for making time for this today. I’m Dr. Reyes, a perinatal-mental-health clinician. Over the next few minutes we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS—to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days; no right or wrong answers, just whatever is true for you. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me you might harm yourself or someone else, in which case we’ll talk together about extra support. We’ll go one question at a time, and you can pause or ask for clarification whenever you need.

Shall we start?  
Thinking back over the last week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

I’ve still been able to laugh—maybe not as easily as before the baby, but when my partner makes silly faces while changing diapers I find myself giggling. It’s not every moment, but the funny side of things still reaches me.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah, most days I can still laugh—like when the baby lets out a huge burp right as my mom is giving me advice. It catches me off-guard and I chuckle. Maybe not quite as hard as I used to, but the laughter is still there.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to little things—like taking the baby for a short walk in the stroller each afternoon or having my favorite iced coffee once she finally goes down for a nap. They’re small, but they still feel enjoyable to me.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Not really. If she spits up right after I’ve changed her outfit, I might think, “Should I have burped her longer?” but I don’t stay stuck on it. I figure babies just do messy stuff sometimes, and we move on.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I do catch myself worrying for no real reason—like lying in bed wondering if her breathing sounds “normal” even though she’s perfectly fine. It’s not constant, but every couple of days I’ll feel that little knot of worry for a while before I can talk myself down.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, I haven’t had that kind of scared or panicky feeling. A little anxious, sure, but not anything close to panic.
Things have been getting on top of me

Mostly I’m keeping up, but there are moments—like yesterday when she wouldn’t nap and the laundry pile felt huge—when I think, “Whoa, this is a lot.” It passes once I check a couple things off the list, though; I don’t feel completely swamped.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, my sleep’s actually been okay. Once I finally get to bed, I fall asleep pretty easily—exhaustion helps with that. I’m not lying there feeling unhappy or anything.
I have felt sad or miserable
I wouldn’t say I feel sad or miserable—maybe just a little worn-out or “blah” every now and then, but it doesn’t stick around. Overall I still have plenty of okay moments each day.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t cried except for one quick tear-up when a lullaby reminded me of my grandma—happy-sad, really. It was over in a minute, not the kind of crying that comes from feeling unhappy.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts like that at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 6: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

Identified symptoms / concerns  
- Mild, intermittent “knot of worry” without panic (Q4)  
- Occasional sense of being briefly overwhelmed; recovers quickly (Q6)  
- “Worn-out / blah” episodes that remit same day (Q8)  

Consistent patterns  
- Preserved capacity for pleasure, laughter, and future-oriented enjoyment (Q1, Q2)  
- No sustained low mood, tearfulness, sleep–mood link, excessive guilt, or self-harm ideation (Q3, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10)  

Screening significance  
- Sub-clinical anxiety symptoms present; do not meet threshold for likely major postpartum depression at this time  
- No current safety concerns  

Risk factors noted  
- None of the following endorsed: persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, crying spells, mood-related insomnia, worthlessness/guilt, panic, self-harm thoughts
